subject: Production gating and timeline: isolated deployment feasibility sync
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Feasibility input request — isolated/on-prem POC gating

Grace / Marissa —

We finished the first-pass technical assessment for the Acme Health POC and I need a decision on two gating items by EOD Friday so we can commit an RTM for the pilot:

1) Minimal ops footprint: can we accept a single-cluster, single-region on-prem configuration (no HA) for the initial 3-month POC under a documented SLA exception? The infra ask is ~2x engineers for deployment + 1x oncall rotation.

2) Data ingress envelope: Acme is asking for VPN termination into their network vs. our usual VPC-peering. The security team flagged key management (HSM) and audit logs as blockers unless we ship private agents.

Attached: isolation_req_matrix.xlsx shows the minimal requirements and enumerates three exception lanes (temporary SLA, reduced telemetry retention, no cross-region failover). Also added a short minimal-footprint-proposal.pdf in the Drive link for quick read.

What I'm asking from Product (Grace): can we accept reduced observability (30-day traces, token-level logs off) for POC to reduce ops load? What are the product guardrails we need (rollback criteria, quality gates, model pinning) to sign off?

What I'm asking from CS (Marissa): can your team take customer comms and manage expectations if we ship with the SLA exception?

Kimberly — can you weigh in on audit evidence we can provide that won't require full SOC packaging?

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: isolation_req_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feasibility input request — isolated/on-prem POC gating

Thanks for the clear write-up, Karthik. Quick responses below and a proposed decision path so we don't block the sales timeline:

- Reduced observability: acceptable for a timeboxed POC only if we get an explicit rollback trigger (quality/regression threshold) and a runbook that the oncall can execute without escalation. Product requirement: model version pinning + deterministic prompt/seed set for latency/quality baseline.

- SLA exception: I can approve a narrow short-term SLA exception (30 days) for the POC, provided Legal signs off and Sales gets written acceptance from Acme that this is a POC, not production. We should capture this in the mutual action plan.

- Ops resourcing: I will reallocate one product engineer to help with the rollout for 4 weeks (hands-on), but we need +1 infra FTE from your team for ongoing anchor support. That means we still need the 2x engineers you listed. Product can cover the program management side for the POC.

Action items (proposal):
  1) Kimberly to confirm minimal audit artifacts we can send (logs, access list, config snapshots).
  2) Karthik to produce a short runbook (15–20 min read) for rollback and incident triage.
  3) Marissa to update Acme comms and get signed POC acknowlegement.
  4) I will draft the product-side acceptance criteria for sign-off (quality and latency thresholds).

If we get all four done by Friday 17:00 PDT I will sign the exception and inform Legal to prepare a limited addendum.

On timeline: Acme's Sales rep said they want to start the POC week of 7/25. That gives us two weeks for the work above. Not a lot of slack, so let's keep items tight.

Thanks —
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Director, Product Management (Deployments)
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-11T11:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feasibility input request — isolated/on-prem POC gating

Short note on audit artifacts — we can provide the following for a POC without full SOC:
- Access control list export (who/when)
- Config snapshot (immutable config hashes)
- Tokenized request/response samples (redacted)
- Container image provenance and SBOMs

We cannot reasonably provide HSM-managed keys onsite unless we coordinate with Acme's hardware team; for the POC we can recommend customer-managed KMS with temporary credentials and short key rotation. That reduces our exposure.

I'll create a small checklist and link it in JIRA INF-3421 (see link). Karthik, please add the runbook there and ping me when it's up — I can then export the artifacts package.

—Kimberly
Security & Compliance (Prod Security)
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Nguyen <sara@acmehealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-07-11T13:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feasibility input request — isolated/on-prem POC gating

Thanks — this is helpful. From Acme's side: we can accept a POC with the following constraints:

- VPN termination is fine for the POC, but we need a documented key-handling approach and a single HMAC-based verification token.
- 30-day telemetry retention is acceptable for the pilot; full audit artifacts must be provided at the end of the POC for our internal compliance review.
- We will sign a POC acknowledgement letter stating this is not production and will list the rollback/quality triggers we agreed on in a shared doc.

I'll have legal draft the acknowledgement and upload it to your Drive folder by Thursday. Please confirm the minimal artifact list (Kimberly's checklist) and the runbook so Acme can map internal oncall to yours for the pilot.

—Sara Nguyen
Head of Engineering, Acme Health
